title: What Counts Toward a High-Deductible Plan Letter's Annual Deductible
content:
On a policy under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies the liability counting toward a high-deductible plan letter's annual deductible is measured from the claim record over the 12 months to date, and entries standing against the paid lines of those months reduce it.

1. **Where entries stand both restating lines of the 12 months to date and recording money recovered from the policyholder on them** — what counts is the liability the paid lines record less what all those entries take back.
2. **Where entries stand restating lines of those months and none records money recovered from the policyholder** — what counts is that liability less what the restatements take back.
3. **Where neither of those holds** — what counts is the liability the paid lines of those months record.

### Reading the three cases

The window is the same in every case: the 12 months to date. What differs is what is taken off the liability the paid lines of those months record.

The first case requires both kinds of entry against the lines of those months, and takes off what all of them take back together. The second requires restatements with no entry recording money recovered from the policyholder, and takes off only what the restatements take back. Where no restatement of those months stands at all, the third case governs and nothing is taken off, whatever else the claim record carries.

### Hypothetical figures

The paid lines of the 12 months to date record liability of 3200.00; restatements of those lines take back 400.00 and entries recording money recovered from the policyholder take back 150.00: what counts is 3200.00 less both, being 2650.00.

The same liability of 3200.00 with restatements taking back 400.00 and no entry recording money recovered from the policyholder: what counts is 2800.00.

The same liability of 3200.00 with no restatement of those months standing: what counts is 3200.00.
